hypotheses.paper: Richards' theorem MR143186 and the line-to-puncture injectivity (l.1544)
hypotheses.note: GX.BTZLine.CountableLinesInput (countably many lines in RichardsInput's setting); proved equivalent to GX.BTZMax.RichardsInput, so RichardsInput's third ingredient (second countability of each line) is discharged

findings: BTZ_1.tex l.1546: « Δ admits a Riemannian metric and is thus second countable » is correct for a connected Hausdorff (ℝ,ℝ)-manifold, and is proved without a metric: unit-speed paths are unique (Hausdorff) and extend along every chart, so a component is the image of an open subset of ℝ under a continuous flow (GX.BTZLine.isLindelof_connectedComponent, secondCountable_connectedComponent, secondCountable_of_connectedSpace). Hausdorffness is used. It holds for every E₀-manifold, with no second countability of the ambient manifold assumed.

BTZ_1.tex l.1545: « a connected component Δ of sing₀(M) » should read sing₀(M̄): the sentence speaks of the E≥0-structure of M̄ and the previous one of the lines of M̄ ∖ M. The Lean statement covers any E₀-manifold, so it covers both readings.

BTZ_1.tex l.1545–1546: the (G, sing(E₀))-structure is read off GX.E0AbsMax.e0Loop_localForm. Every element of the model groupoid is (τ, z) ↦ (τ + a, R z) near an axis point, so the line charts (the height τ of the paper chart) change by translations. The orientation question of OQ-150 (d) (whether R may be a reflection) does not matter here: R fixes 0.

BTZ_1.tex l.1544–1546: GX.BTZMax.RichardsInput (« sing₀ is Lindelöf ») is equivalent to « countably many lines » (GX.BTZLine.richardsInput_iff_countableLines, through isLindelof_S0_iff_countable). The only unproved content left in the second bullet is therefore Richards' theorem together with the line-to-puncture injectivity.

BTZ_1.tex l.395–396 (btzcor:manifold_smooth_manifold_singular), at E₀ where sing = sing₀: the topological half of the second sentence is proved (GX.BTZLine.btz_line_structure). sing₀ is closed. It is locally flat: in the paper chart at each of its points it is exactly the axis. It is a topological 1-manifold with an (ℝ,ℝ)-structure, and each component is second countable. The smooth 3-manifold structure is not attempted, and neither is sing_α for α > 0.
questions: « closed 1-submanifold » (l.395) is read topologically: closed, and the axis in a chart of the E₀-atlas (local flatness), carrying a 1-manifold atlas. The smooth reading is not formalized (no smooth structure on M exists in the library).
« (ℝ,ℝ)-structure » (l.1546) is read as a (G,X)-structure in the sense of GX.gxGroupoid, with G = Multiplicative ℝ acting on X = ℝ by translation. This is the library's DEC-16 form.

kb_proposals: A Hausdorff ChartedSpace ℝ X with HasGroupoid X (gxGroupoid (Multiplicative ℝ) ℝ) has Lindelöf, second countable components: GX.BTZLine.isLindelof_connectedComponent / secondCountable_connectedComponent (unit-speed flow, no metric).

sing₀ of any E₀-manifold is a ChartedSpace ℝ with a translation structure: instances GX.BTZLine.instChartedSpaceS0 and instHasGroupoidS0, with chart lineChart x = the τ of E0CBG.paperChart x; and paperChart_mem_axis_iff says sing₀ is the axis in every paper chart.
GX.BTZMax.RichardsInput ↔ GX.BTZLine.CountableLinesInput (richardsInput_iff_countableLines): the line second countability is discharged, and only « countably many lines » remains cited.

Translation action: for g : Multiplicative ℝ, g • y = Multiplicative.toAdd g + y holds by rfl (mathlib's Multiplicative.mulAction from AddAction ℝ ℝ); ContinuousConstSMul (Multiplicative ℝ) ℝ is found by inferInstance.
